title: The Indus Valley Civilization: Bronze Age Urban Genius

questions.question: Harappa was excavated in 1921 by:
questions.rationale: Daya Ram Sahni excavated Harappa in 1921; R. D. Banerji followed with Mohenjo-daro in 1922, and John Marshall, ASI Director-General, announced the discoveries in 1924.

questions.question: The Harappan site famous for its dockyard is:
questions.rationale: Lothal in Gujarat has a brick-lined basin 216 m by 37 m interpreted as a dockyard, and also yielded a bead factory and a terracotta toy ship.

questions.question: The earliest ploughed field ever attested archaeologically comes from:
questions.rationale: Kalibangan on the Ghaggar in Rajasthan yielded a ploughed field — the world's earliest attested — along with rows of fire altars.

questions.question: Harappan baked bricks followed a standardised ratio of:
questions.rationale: Baked bricks in the fixed ratio 1 : 2 : 4, laid in English bond, were used across every settlement from Harappa to Lothal — a hallmark of Harappan standardisation.

questions.question: The Great Bath, a bitumen-waterproofed tank 11.88 m by 7.01 m, belongs to:
questions.rationale: The Great Bath is the most famous citadel structure of Mohenjo-daro — a sunken ritual tank 2.43 m deep with steps at both ends.

questions.question: In Mesopotamian records, the Indus region was called:
questions.rationale: Texts of Sargon of Akkad mention ships from Meluhha, the Indus land; Dilmun (Bahrain) and Magan (Oman) were the trade middlemen.

questions.question: The bronze Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-daro was made using which technique?
questions.rationale: The 10.5 cm Dancing Girl was cast in bronze by the lost-wax method, showing the advanced metallurgy of the Mature Harappan phase.

questions.question: Harappan weights were based mainly on which system?
questions.rationale: Chert cube weights follow a binary series — 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 — with larger units in decimal multiples such as 16, 160, and 320.

questions.question: Why does the Harappan script remain undeciphered?
options: It has too many signs to classify
No bilingual text exists and the language family is unknown
It was written only on perishable material
questions.rationale: With roughly 400-600 short signs, no bilingual text, and an unknown language family, every claimed decipherment — Sanskrit or Dravidian — remains hypothesis.

questions.question: Which decline theory is now largely doubted by archaeologists?
options: Aryan invasion as argued by Mortimer Wheeler
questions.rationale: Wheeler's invasion reading rested on Mohenjo-daro skeletons, but these span decades with no massacre layer; climate and river-shift theories are now better supported.
